rule MSSP_T1003_001_LSASS_Minidump_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects creation of a minidump file whose path or name references LSASS, indicating an adversary has dumped LSASS process memory to disk. This fires on the resulting file artifact rather than the process command line, providing coverage against tools that suppress or obfuscate their command-line arguments. Covers procdump, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, custom dumpers, and WerFault-based silent-exit abuse."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file-creation telemetry (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon, Carbon Black, Sysmon Event ID 11). The sensor must record the full target file path at creation time."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate Windows Error Reporting (WER) crash dumps for lsass.exe generated by the OS after an unexpected LSASS crash (rare and should be investigated regardless). Authorized memory forensics or incident-response tooling run by the security team. Some endpoint protection products perform supervised LSASS snapshots for tamper detection."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good dump output directories used by your IR tooling to %global_allowed_dump_paths. Add authorized dump-writer process paths (e.g., your EDR sensor binary) to %global_allowed_dump_writers. Raise severity to Critical and page on-call if the writing process is not a recognized security tool."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Match any file whose full path contains an lsass-related token
    // Covers: lsass.dmp, lsass_dump.dmp, lsass.mdmp, lsassdump, lsass_mem, etc.
    $file.target.file.full_path = /lsass/ nocase

    // Restrict to minidump / raw memory dump extensions commonly produced by
    // procdump (.dmp, .mdmp), comsvcs MiniDump (.dmp), and custom dumpers (.bin, .dat, .raw).
    // Broad enough to survive attacker extension renaming when combined with the name filter.
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(dmp|mdmp|bin|dat|raw|dump|mem)$/ nocase

    // Exclude known-good paths and writers via reference lists for MSSP multi-tenant tuning
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_dump_paths
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_dump_writers

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $dump_file_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $writing_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_001_LSASS_OpenProcess_Then_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects a non-system process opening a handle to lsass.exe followed by creation of a dump or suspicious binary file on the same host within 10 minutes. This correlation catches memory-dump tooling that does not rely on named utilities, covering cases where the attacker renames their binary. The first event captures the PROCESS_OPEN against lsass; the second captures the resulting dump file being written to disk."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN events with target process name populated (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint via Chronicle ingestion, or Sysmon Event ID 10). Also requires FILE_CREATION events with full path (Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent EDR)."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate crash-dump collection by Windows Error Reporting (WerFault.exe), authorised vulnerability scanners, endpoint security products performing integrity checks, and some backup agents that snapshot process state. Tune using the reference lists below."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised dump-collection parent process paths to %global_allowed_lsass_openers. Add approved dump output directories (e.g., corporate crash-dump shares) to %global_allowed_dump_paths. Consider raising severity to Critical and lowering the time window if your EDR reliably emits PROCESS_OPEN for lsass."

  events:
    // --- Leg 1: A process opens a handle to lsass.exe ---
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    // Target of the open must be lsass
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase
    // Exclude the OS itself and known-good security tooling via reference list
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_lsass_openers
    // Exclude common Windows system paths that legitimately open lsass
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\(svchost|csrss|wininit|services|lsm|smss)\.exe$/ nocase
    // Bind the joining key
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Leg 2: A dump or suspicious file is created on the same host ---
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    // Match common dump extensions and generic binary drops in writable locations
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(dmp|mdmp|bin|dat|zip|7z|gz)$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(temp|tmp|appdata|public|programdata|users\\[^\\]+\\documents)/ nocase
    )
    // Exclude known-good dump output paths (e.g., authorised crash-dump directories)
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_dump_paths
    // Exclude Windows Error Reporting's own output directory when WER is the writer
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\WerFault\.exe$/ nocase
    // Bind the joining key
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Chronological ordering: open must precede file creation ---
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $opener_process = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $dump_file_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $opener_pid = array_distinct($open.principal.process.pid)

  condition:
    $open and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_002_SAM_Registry_Hive_Exported_To_File {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects file creation events consistent with the SAM or SYSTEM registry hive being saved to disk via reg.exe or volume shadow copy access. Adversaries export HKLM\\SAM and HKLM\\SYSTEM to offline files to extract credential hashes without triggering command-line detections. This rule fires on the resulting file artifact rather than the process command line, providing a complementary detection layer."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file telemetry (e.g., CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Carbon Black) or Sysmon Event ID 11 (FileCreate) forwarded to Chronicle. The creating process field must be populated."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Authorised backup agents (e.g., Windows Server Backup, Veeam, Acronis) that snapshot registry hives. Domain join or imaging workflows that legitimately export registry hives. Security tooling performing authorised credential audits."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup agent process paths to %global_allowed_hive_backup_processes. Add known-safe destination directories (e.g., dedicated backup shares) to %global_allowed_hive_backup_paths. Scope by hostname group for servers running scheduled backup jobs."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // The written file must reside outside the canonical Windows registry backing-store
    // locations. Legitimate hive files live under System32\config; any copy elsewhere
    // is suspicious. We also catch writes directly into temp, user-writable, or
    // attacker-favoured staging directories.
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(sam|system|security|ntds)(\.hiv|\.hive|\.bak|\.sav|\.reg|\.dmp|\.dat)?$/ nocase

    // Exclude the canonical registry backing-store path where Windows itself writes hives.
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\config\\/ nocase

    // Exclude Volume Shadow Copy provider paths (VSS internal writes are expected there).
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\sru\\/ nocase

    // The process writing the file should not be a known-safe backup agent.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_hive_backup_processes

    // Require a principal hostname to be present (filters noise from incomplete telemetry).
    $file.principal.hostname != ""

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $written_file = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_002_SAM_Registry_Read_Then_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects a two-stage SAM credential theft pattern: a process opens the SAM or SYSTEM registry hive (registry read/access event) followed by creation of a file with a SAM or SYSTEM dump name in a suspicious path on the same host within 10 minutes. This covers in-memory registry extraction tools that do not invoke reg.exe on the command line, providing additive coverage beyond process-launch command-line rules."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR registry telemetry (REGISTRY_MODIFICATION or FILE_READ events for HKLM\\SAM / HKLM\\SYSTEM) and EDR file-creation telemetry. Sysmon Event IDs 12/13 (registry) and 11 (file create) are sufficient. Windows Security Event 4663 (object access on SAM) also populates the registry event."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Backup software performing VSS-based registry exports; authorised SCCM/Intune imaging workflows; domain join operations writing local account data; security tooling performing credential hygiene checks."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup and imaging process paths to %global_allowed_sam_readers. Add known-good destination directories (e.g. backup share staging paths) to %global_allowed_sam_dump_paths. Narrow the file name regex if your environment uses a specific naming convention for authorised exports."

  events:
    // Stage 1: process reads/accesses the SAM or SYSTEM registry hive
    $reg.metadata.event_type = "REGISTRY_MODIFICATION"
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /\\(SAM|SYSTEM)(\\|$)/ nocase
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /^HKLM/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_sam_readers
    $reg.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: a file with a SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY dump name is created on the same host
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /(\\|\/)(sam|system|security|ntds|hklm_sam|hklm_sys)(\.hiv|\.save|\.bak|\.dmp|\.bin|\.dat|\.tmp)?$/  nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_sam_dump_paths
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_sam_readers
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: registry access must precede file creation
    $reg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($reg.principal.hostname)
    $registry_keys_accessed = array_distinct($reg.target.registry.registry_key)
    $dump_files_created = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $dumping_processes = array_distinct($reg.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $file_writing_processes = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $reg and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_003_NTDS_File_Read_Or_Copy_Artifact {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects file read or access events targeting the NTDS.dit database or its associated transaction log files (edb.log, edb*.log) outside of expected NTDS service paths. Attackers staging a copy of NTDS.dit via Volume Shadow Copy, ntdsutil, or direct file access will produce a FILE_READ or FILE_CREATION event against these paths. This rule targets the resulting file artifact rather than the command line, providing coverage orthogonal to process-creation detections."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: NTDS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file telemetry (e.g., CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) or Windows Security audit policy with Object Access auditing enabled on NTDS.dit (SACL). Chronicle must ingest file-level events mapped to FILE_READ or FILE_CREATION UDM event types."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services (lsass.exe, ntdsa.dll) performing routine reads of NTDS.dit; legitimate backup agents (Windows Server Backup, Veeam, Commvault) accessing VSS snapshots; NTDS defragmentation via ntdsutil performing offline maintenance. Tune using %ntds_allowed_readers."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %ntds_allowed_readers with the full paths of authorised backup agent executables and the NTDS service binary (e.g., C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe, C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntdsa.dll). Scope the rule to domain controller asset groups if your SIEM supports asset tagging. Consider raising severity to Critical and auto-escalating if the reading process is not in the allow list."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target must be the NTDS database file or its associated ESE transaction logs
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\ntds\.dit$/i nocase or
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\ntds\\edb.*\.log$/i nocase or
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\ntds\\edb\.chk$/i nocase or
    // Also catch copies staged in temp, user-writable, or VSS snapshot paths
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(temp|tmp|appdata|users|public|programdata)\\.*ntds\.dit$/i nocase or
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\device\\harddiskvolumeshadowcopy[0-9]+\\.*ntds\.dit$/ nocase

    // Exclude the legitimate NTDS service reader processes
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %ntds_allowed_readers

    // Exclude the canonical NTDS directory as the source process working path
    // to avoid alerting on the NTDS service itself doing internal I/O
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\windows\\system32\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $reading_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_file = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $actor_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_003_NTDS_ShadowCopy_Then_NTDS_FileRead {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects a two-stage NTDS extraction pattern: a Volume Shadow Copy is created or accessed on a host, followed by a file read or creation event targeting the NTDS.dit database file path within a 10-minute window. This covers adversaries who use VSS to bypass file locks on the live NTDS.dit without relying on command-line keyword matching."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: NTDS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file telemetry (FILE_CREATION or FILE_READ events) and process launch telemetry. EDR must log shadow copy service interactions and file access to NTDS paths. Sysmon Event IDs 11 (FileCreate) and 23 (FileDelete) or equivalent EDR file events are required."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate domain controller backup agents (e.g., Windows Server Backup, Veeam, Commvault, Veritas) that snapshot VSS and read NTDS.dit as part of authorised backup jobs. Authorised AD health-check or migration tooling."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup agent process paths to %global_allowed_backup_processes and authorised hostnames to %global_allowed_dc_backup_hosts. Narrow the file event filter if your EDR logs all NTDS directory access at high volume."

  events:
    // Stage 1: A process interacts with the Volume Shadow Copy service or
    // creates a shadow copy - detected via a process launch of vssadmin,
    // wmic, or diskshadow targeting shadow copy creation.
    $vss.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $vss.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(vssadmin|wmic|diskshadow|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/ nocase
    $vss.target.process.command_line = /(shadow|vssadmin|shadowcopy|shadowstorage)/ nocase
    not $vss.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_processes
    not $vss.principal.hostname in %global_allowed_dc_backup_hosts
    $vss.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: A file creation or read event targeting the NTDS.dit file,
    // either from its live location or from a shadow copy mount path.
    // This fires when the adversary copies NTDS.dit out of the VSS snapshot.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /(\\NTDS\\Ntds\.dit|\\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy[0-9]+\\.*\\NTDS\\Ntds\.dit|\\Temp\\.*\.dit|\\Windows\\Temp\\.*\.dit)/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_processes
    not $file.principal.hostname in %global_allowed_dc_backup_hosts
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: shadow copy action must precede the file event
    $vss.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($vss.principal.hostname)

This targets the network-observable side of DCSync rather than process command-line, providing additive coverage to existing PROCESS_LAUNCH rules."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.006"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: DCSync"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires network flow or firewall telemetry showing RPC/SMB connections to domain controllers, AND Windows Security Event 4624/4648 (logon events) or equivalent EDR authentication telemetry. DC hostnames must be populated in the %known_domain_controllers reference list."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate domain controller replication traffic from secondary DCs, Azure AD Connect sync hosts, backup agents performing AD snapshots, privileged admin workstations with scheduled AD queries."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %known_domain_controllers with all DC hostnames/IPs. Add AD Connect servers and authorised replication hosts to %global_allowed_replication_sources. Add service accounts that legitimately authenticate after AD queries to %global_allowed_dc_auth_accounts."

    // Event 1: Non-DC host makes an RPC/SMB connection toward a domain controller
    // DCSync uses MS-DRSR over RPC (port 135 for endpoint mapper, then dynamic high ports, or 445 for SMB transport)
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $net.target.hostname in %known_domain_controllers
    (
      $net.target.port = 135 or
      $net.target.port = 445 or
      ($net.target.port >= 49152 and $net.target.port <= 65535)

    not $net.principal.hostname in %known_domain_controllers

    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.principal.hostname = $src_hostname

      $auth.target.user.userid = /krbtgt/i nocase or
      $auth.target.user.userid = /administrator/i nocase or
      $auth.target.user.userid = /admin/i nocase or
      $auth.target.user.userid = /svc_/i nocase or

Auditd rule example: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S openat -F dir=/proc -F key=proc_mem_access"
    platform = "Linux"

    tuning_guidance = "Add known debugger and profiler paths to %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers. Add security agent process paths (e.g., CrowdStrike sensor, SentinelOne agent) to the same list.   events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // /proc/<pid>/mem  - direct memory read/write interface

    $file.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps|smaps|smaps_rollup|pagemap)$/ nocase

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /^\[/ nocase

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(apt|apt-get|dpkg|rpm|yum|dnf|zypper|snap|flatpak)$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.009")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_proc_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $accessing_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

    description = "Detects Python script files (.py, .pyc, .pyo, .pyw) written to suspicious or high-value filesystem locations (temp directories, user home staging areas, web roots, cron directories, admin shares) by processes other than known package managers or IDEs. Attackers frequently drop Python payloads to disk as a staging step before or instead of interactive execution, making file-creation telemetry an additive detection layer that is harder to suppress than command-line logging."

    platform = "Linux, macOS, Windows, ESXi"
    false_positives = "Legitimate Python package installers (pip, conda, poetry), IDE auto-save operations (VS Code, PyCharm), CI/CD pipeline agents writing test scripts, configuration management tools (Ansible, Salt), software deployment agents."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Match Python script and bytecode extensions across all platforms
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(py|pyc|pyo|pyw)$/ nocase

    // Suspicious destination paths: temp dirs, cron dirs, web roots, home staging,
    // named pipes area, ESXi scratch, world-writable common locations
    $file.target.file.full_path = /(
      [\/\\](tmp|temp|var\/tmp|dev\/shm)[\/\\]|
      [\/\\](www|htdocs|html|webroot|public_html|srv\/http)[\/\\]|
      [\/\\](cron\.(d|daily|hourly|weekly|monthly))[\/\\]|
      [\/\\](etc\/cron)[\/\\]|
      [\/\\]AppData[\/\\](Local|Roaming)[\/\\]Temp[\/\\]|

      [\/\\]home[\/\\][^\/\\]+[\/\\]\.(config|cache|local)[\/\\]|
      [\/\\]vmfs[\/\\]volumes[\/\\]|
      [\/\\]scratch[\/\\]|

    $file

    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = /(\/|\\)(sh|bash|zsh|dash|ksh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|curl|wget|busybox)$/ nocase
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_python_parents
    not $proc.principal.hostname in %python_allowed_orchestration_hosts

    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects modification of network device startup or running configuration files, a state-change artifact produced when an adversary abuses the network CLI to alter device behavior. Targets the resulting file write rather than the CLI invocation itself, providing coverage that survives command-line logging evasion. Covers changes to startup-config, running-config, and equivalent persistent configuration stores on routers, switches, and firewalls."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.008"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Network Device CLI"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires file-system telemetry from network device EDR agents (e.g., Cisco Secure Endpoint on IOS-XE), syslog-derived UDM events from SIEM connectors that surface config-write operations as FILE_MODIFICATION, or network device management platform audit logs (e.g., Cisco DNA Center, Juniper Junos Space) forwarded to Chronicle."
    platform = "Network Devices (Cisco IOS/IOS-XE/NX-OS, Juniper JunOS, Palo Alto PAN-OS, Fortinet FortiOS)"
    false_positives = "Authorized network engineers performing planned change-window configuration pushes; automated configuration management tools (Ansible, Terraform, NAPALM, Cisco NSO); backup jobs that write config snapshots; zero-touch provisioning workflows."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %network_device_config_allowed_principals with service accounts and hostnames used by authorized automation and change-management tooling. Populate %network_device_allowed_config_paths with any non-standard config file paths specific to your environment. Consider narrowing the match window to business hours if after-hours changes are always unauthorized."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_MODIFICATION"

    // Match well-known network OS configuration file paths and names.
    // Covers startup-config, running-config, candidate configs, and
    // platform-specific equivalents across major vendors.
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/:]startup[\-_]config/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/:]running[\-_]config/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/:]candidate[\-_]config/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/:]system[\-_]config/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /nvram:\/startup/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /flash:[\/\\].*\.cfg$/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /bootflash:[\/\\].*\.cfg$/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/config\/running/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/config\/startup/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/opt\/pancfg\/mgmt\/saved-configs\//i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/data\/config\/.*\.conf$/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/etc\/config\/.*\.conf$/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /juniper\.conf/i nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\/config\/db\/factory-junos/i nocase
    )

    // Exclude paths explicitly allow-listed for this environment
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %network_device_allowed_config_paths

    // Exclude principals (users or processes) that are authorized to write configs
    not $file.principal.user.userid in %network_device_config_allowed_principals

    // Exclude known automation hostnames performing scheduled config management
    not $file.principal.hostname in %network_device_config_allowed_principals

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.008")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $modified_config_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)
    $acting_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

    not $auth.principal.ip in %network_mgmt_plane_sources

  meta:

    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects an AutoIT or AutoHotKey interpreter (or compiled script) spawning a child process that subsequently establishes an outbound network connection. This sequence is characteristic of malicious automation scripts used for payload delivery, C2 beaconing, or keylogger exfiltration. Variant 2 of 2 for T1059.010 - complements the process-creation/command-line rule by correlating process lineage with network activity."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.010"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: AutoHotKey & AutoIT"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR process telemetry (PROCESS_LAUNCH) and network telemetry (NETWORK_CONNECTION) with principal.process.file.full_path populated. Sysmon Event IDs 1 and 3, or equivalent EDR events ingested into Chronicle UDM."
    platform = "Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate AutoIT-packaged software installers that phone home for updates (e.g., bundled AutoIT runtimes in commercial software). AutoHotKey scripts used by helpdesk or power users for legitimate automation that access internal services. Software testing frameworks using AutoIT for UI automation."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good AutoIT/AHK parent process paths to %global_allowed_autoscript_parents. Add approved internal network destinations to %rfc1918_internal to suppress internal-only connections. Narrow by target.port if only specific exfiltration ports are of concern. Consider raising risk_score if target.port is 443 or 80 combined with non-browser child processes."

  events:
    // Event 1: AutoIT or AutoHotKey interpreter spawns a child process
    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    // Match AutoIT interpreter, AutoHotKey interpreter, or compiled script wrappers
    // au3.exe = AutoIT script runner, autoit3.exe = standard interpreter,
    // autohotkey.exe / ahk2exe.exe = AHK runtime and compiler
    $proc.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(autoit3|au3|autohotkey|ahk2exe|autohotkeyu32|autohotkeyx32|autohotkeyx64)\.exe$/  nocase
    // Child process must not itself be another script interpreter (avoid chained interpreter noise)
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path != ""
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_autoscript_parents
    // Capture the hostname as the join key
    $proc.principal.hostname = $hostname
    // Capture the child process path to correlate with the network event
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = $child_proc_path

    // Event 2: The spawned child process makes an outbound network connection
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    // The network event must originate from the same child process that was launched
    $net.principal.process.file.full_path = $child_proc_path
    $net.principal.hostname = $hostname
    // Exclude loopback and link-local to focus on meaningful outbound activity
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    not $net.target.ip = "127.0.0.1"
    not $net.target.ip = "::1"

    // Chronological ordering: process launch must precede the network connection
    $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $child_proc_path over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.010")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($proc.principal.hostname)
    $autoscript_interpreter = array_distinct($proc.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $spawned_child_process = array_distinct($proc.target.process.file.full_path)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $event_count = count($net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $proc and $net
}

    description = "Detects unexpected file creation or modification within the Docker daemon socket directory or container runtime configuration paths. Adversaries interacting with the Docker API or CLI produce artifact-level state changes in socket-adjacent config files, overlay filesystem layers, and container metadata directories. This rule targets the resulting file artifact rather than the command line, providing coverage that survives command-line log evasion."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.013"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires host-level file integrity or EDR telemetry that captures FILE_CREATION and FILE_MODIFICATION events on Linux container hosts (e.g., Falco, Sysdig, CrowdStrike Falcon, or equivalent agent forwarding to Chronicle)."
    platform = "Containers, Linux"
    false_positives = "Legitimate Docker daemon operations during container start/stop cycles, CI/CD pipeline runners (Jenkins, GitLab Runner, GitHub Actions self-hosted), container orchestration agents (Kubernetes kubelet, containerd), and authorised DevOps tooling that manages container runtime state."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known CI/CD runner process paths to %global_allowed_container_runtime_writers. Add orchestration agent hostnames to %global_allowed_container_hosts. Narrow severity by correlating with non-business-hours or non-pipeline user context."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target paths that represent Docker/container runtime state artifacts:
    // - /var/lib/docker overlay2 layers (new image or container layer materialised)
    // - /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/ metadata files written when a container is created/exec'd
    // - /run/docker/ and /var/run/docker/ socket-adjacent control files
    // - /etc/docker/ config changes (daemon.json, certs)
    // - containerd state directory
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/lib\/docker\/(overlay2|containers|volumes|tmp)\// nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/run\/docker\// nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/run\/docker\// nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/etc\/docker\// nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/lib\/containerd\// nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/run\/containerd\// nocase
    )

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(kubelet|crio|podman|buildkitd|systemd|init)$/ nocase

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_container_runtime_writers

    not $file.principal.hostname in %global_allowed_container_hosts

    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $artifact_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1071_003_Mail_Protocol_Artifact_Written_By_Non_Mail_Process {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file artifacts characteristic of mail-protocol C2 activity: a process that is NOT a recognised mail client or mail daemon writes a file whose path or name matches common mail spool, mailbox, or mail-library staging locations. Adversaries abusing SMTP/IMAP/POP3 for C2 often drop helper scripts, configuration blobs, or captured mail artefacts into these directories as a side-effect of their tooling. This rule fires on the resulting FILE_CREATION or FILE_MODIFICATION event rather than on process command-line arguments, providing a complementary detection layer that is harder to evade."
    mitre_tactic         = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique      = "T1071.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: Mail Protocols"
    log_prerequisites    = "Requires EDR file-telemetry (e.g. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Sysmon Event ID 11) forwarded to Chronicle. The writing process path must be populated in principal.process.file.full_path."
    platform             = "Linux, macOS, Windows"
    false_positives      = "Legitimate MUA/MDA upgrades writing to mail spool; custom in-house mail relay agents; backup agents archiving mailboxes; antivirus quarantine of mail attachments; mail migration tooling."
    tuning_guidance      = "Add authorised mail-related process paths to %global_allowed_mail_processes and authorised mail-staging directories to %global_allowed_mail_paths. Narrow scope further by restricting to specific high-value asset groups via principal.hostname prefix lists."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target path matches mail spool, mailbox, or mail-library staging locations
    // Covers: /var/spool/mail, /var/mail, /var/mbox, Maildir structures,
    //         Windows mail profile stores, macOS Mail.app data directories,
    //         and generic .eml / .mbox / .msg staging files anywhere on disk.
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\]var[\/\\](spool[\/\\]mail|mail)[\/\\]/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\](Maildir|cur|new|tmp)[\/\\][^\/\\]+$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(eml|mbox|msg|mbx)$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\]AppData[\/\\].*[\/\\](Outlook|Thunderbird|Mailspring|Mutt)[\/\\]/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\]Library[\/\\]Mail[\/\\]/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\]\.(?:mutt|muttrc|offlineimap|msmtp|fetchmail)/ nocase
    )

    // Writing process is NOT a recognised, legitimate mail agent.
    // Legitimate mail processes (sendmail, postfix, dovecot, mutt, thunderbird,
    // outlook, evolution, fetchmail, offlineimap, etc.) are excluded via reference list.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_mail_processes

    // Exclude common system maintenance processes that legitimately touch mail paths
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /[\/\\](logrotate|rsync|tar|cp|mv|install|rpm|dpkg|yum|apt|brew|msiexec|svchost)(\.(exe))?$/ nocase

    // Exclude backup and AV agents
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /[\/\\](veeam|backup|acronis|clam|defender|msmpeng|mbam)(.*)?(\.(exe))?$/ nocase

    // Require a writing process to be identified (avoids noisy kernel-attributed events)
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path != ""

    // Exclude paths already covered by the reference list for allowed staging areas
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_mail_paths

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.003")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $writing_process   = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $artifact_path     = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $net.target.port in [25, 110, 143, 465, 587, 993, 995]

rule MSSP_T1071_004_DNS_Tunnel_Config_File_Artifact {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects file creation or modification of DNS resolver/stub configuration files in non-standard or user-writable locations, which may indicate a DNS tunneling tool writing its configuration, cache, or pipe file. Attackers deploying DNS C2 frameworks (e.g., dnscat2, iodine, dns2tcp) frequently write configuration, socket, or log artifacts to disk. This rule targets the resulting file artifact rather than the process command line, providing coverage orthogonal to process-launch detections."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: DNS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file telemetry (e.g., CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Sysmon Event ID 11) forwarded to Chronicle via UDM. FILE_CREATION and FILE_MODIFICATION events must be populated with target.file.full_path."
    platform = "Linux, macOS, Windows"
    false_positives = "Legitimate DNS client libraries writing cache files, VPN clients that manage local DNS stubs, network diagnostic tools (e.g., dig, nslookup output redirects), custom resolvers in containerised environments, developer tooling such as dnsmasq or unbound writing to non-standard paths."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths to %global_allowed_dns_config_writers. Add approved directories to %global_allowed_dns_artifact_dirs. Narrow the file extension regex if your environment uses a specific DNS tool that generates false positives."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target paths that DNS tunneling tools commonly write to:
    // - Hidden files or dot-prefixed names in home/tmp directories
    // - Files with dns, tunnel, tun, iodine, dnscat, d2tcp in the name
    // - Named pipes or socket-like files in /tmp or /var/tmp
    // - Windows: AppData, Temp, or ProgramData paths with dns-related names
    // - Generic: any file with a .dns extension written outside system dirs
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\](\.dns|\.iodine|\.dnscat|dnscat|iodine|dns2tcp|d2tcp|dnstun|dnsproxy|dnsrelay)[^\/\\]*$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\](tmp|temp|appdata|programdata)[\/\\][^\/\\]*(dns|tunnel|tun)[^\/\\]*\.(cfg|conf|ini|log|dat|tmp|cache|sock|pipe)$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\]\.[a-z0-9]{4,16}\.(dns|dnsc|dnst)$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\/\\](home|users)[\/\\][^\/\\]+[\/\\]\.(dns|iodine|dnscat|dnstunnel)[\/\\]/ nocase
    )

    // Exclude known system-level DNS configuration paths that are legitimately written
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/etc\/(resolv\.conf|hosts|nsswitch\.conf|systemd\/resolved\.conf)$/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/cache\/(nscd|bind|named)\// nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/run\/systemd\/resolve\// nocase

    // Exclude known-good writers via reference list
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_dns_config_writers

    // Exclude system-level processes that legitimately touch DNS config
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /[\/\\](systemd-resolved|named|unbound|dnsmasq|nscd|avahi-daemon|NetworkManager|svchost)\.exe$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $artifact_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $writing_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1071_004_DNS_Beacon_High_Entropy_Then_Network {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects DNS tunneling / beaconing by correlating an anomalous DNS query (long or high-subdomain-count hostname queried by a non-browser process) followed by a subsequent network connection from the same host to the same resolved destination. This targets the C2 channel behaviour rather than the tool used to create it, providing additive coverage beyond process-launch command-line rules."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: DNS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires DNS query telemetry mapped to NETWORK_DNS (e.g. Zeek dns.log, Windows DNS debug log, EDR DNS events) AND network flow or connection telemetry mapped to NETWORK_CONNECTION. Both must populate principal.hostname and the DNS question/answer fields."
    platform = "ESXi, Linux, macOS, Network Devices, Windows"
    false_positives = "CDN pre-fetch traffic, software update services with long hostnames (e.g. Windows Update, Akamai), telemetry pipelines, security tools performing reputation lookups, legitimate use of DNS-over-HTTPS bypass tools."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good high-entropy domains to %dns_tunnel_allowed_domains. Add approved internal resolvers or update service FQDNs. Raise the subdomain-depth regex threshold or restrict to specific process names via %dns_tunnel_allowed_processes if false-positive rate is high in a specific environment."

  events:
    // --- Leg 1: Suspicious DNS query ---
    // A DNS lookup for a hostname that is either extremely long (>50 chars in
    // the leftmost label, characteristic of data-encoded subdomains) OR
    // contains four or more subdomain labels (deep nesting used by tunnels).
    // We exclude common CDN / update patterns via reference list.
    $dns.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_DNS"
    (
      $dns.network.dns.questions.name = /^[a-z0-9_\-]{50,}\./  nocase
      or
      $dns.network.dns.questions.name = /^[^.]+\.[^.]+\.[^.]+\.[^.]+\.[^.]+/  nocase
    )
    not $dns.network.dns.questions.name in %dns_tunnel_allowed_domains
    not $dns.principal.process.file.full_path in %dns_tunnel_allowed_processes
    $dns.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Leg 2: Outbound network connection following the DNS query ---
    // The same host makes an outbound connection shortly after the suspicious
    // DNS lookup. We restrict to non-RFC-1918 destinations to focus on
    // external C2 and exclude common high-volume internal ports.
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    not $net.target.ip in %dns_tunnel_allowed_ips
    $net.target.port != 80
    $net.target.port != 443
    $net.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: DNS query must precede the connection
    $dns.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($dns.principal.hostname)
    $suspicious_dns_names = array_distinct($dns.network.dns.questions.name)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $initiating_processes = array_distinct($dns.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $dns_event_count = count($dns.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $dns and $net
}

rule MSSP_T1071_005_PubSub_Process_Then_External_Network {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a non-browser, non-messaging process that first opens a connection on a known pub/sub broker port (MQTT:1883/8883, AMQP:5671/5672, XMPP:5222/5269, STOMP:61613/61614) and then establishes a sustained external network flow on the same port within 5 minutes. This pattern is additive to process-launch command-line rules and focuses on the network behaviour of an already-running process communicating over pub/sub protocols to an external broker."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: Publish/Subscribe Protocols"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or host-based network telemetry producing both NETWORK_CONNECTION and NETWORK_FLOW events with principal.process populated. Sysmon EventID 3, Zeek conn.log forwarded via Chronicle ingestion, or equivalent EDR network events."
    platform = "Windows, Linux, macOS, Network Devices"
    false_positives = "Legitimate IoT management agents, MQTT-based monitoring tools (e.g., Mosquitto clients), enterprise messaging middleware (RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ client processes), chat clients using XMPP, CI/CD pipeline agents using AMQP queues."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good process paths to %global_allowed_pubsub_processes. Add approved internal broker IPs/ranges to %global_allowed_pubsub_destinations. Raise the risk score threshold for internet-routable destinations only."

  events:
    // Leg 1: Process initiates a NETWORK_CONNECTION on a pub/sub port to an external host
    $conn.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    (
      $conn.target.port = 1883 or
      $conn.target.port = 8883 or
      $conn.target.port = 5671 or
      $conn.target.port = 5672 or
      $conn.target.port = 5222 or
      $conn.target.port = 5269 or
      $conn.target.port = 61613 or
      $conn.target.port = 61614

    // Exclude RFC-1918 destinations - external broker only

    // Exclude known-good pub/sub client processes
    not $conn.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_pubsub_processes
    // Exclude browser processes that may use these ports incidentally
    not $conn.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(chrome|firefox|msedge|safari|opera|brave)\.exe$/ nocase
    $conn.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $conn.target.port = $pubsub_port

    $flow.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_FLOW"
    (
      $flow.target.port = 1883 or
      $flow.target.port = 8883 or
      $flow.target.port = 5671 or
      $flow.target.port = 5672 or
      $flow.target.port = 5222 or
      $flow.target.port = 5269 or
      $flow.target.port = 61613 or
      $flow.target.port = 61614
    )
    not $flow.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal

    not $flow.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(chrome|firefox|msedge|safari|opera|brave)\.exe$/ nocase
    $flow.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $flow.target.port = $pubsub_port

    // Chronological ordering: connection must precede or coincide with flow record
    $conn.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $pubsub_port over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.005")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($conn.principal.hostname)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($conn.target.ip)
    $observed_ports = array_distinct($conn.target.port)
    $initiating_processes = array_distinct($conn.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $flow_bytes_sent = max($flow.network.sent_bytes)
    $flow_bytes_received = max($flow.network.received_bytes)

  condition:
    $conn and $flow
}

    $auth.target.user.userid != ""

    (

    false_positives = "VPN split-tunneling causing IP churn, corporate NAT pools with multiple egress IPs, mobile users switching between Wi-Fi and cellular, shared service accounts used by automation from multiple hosts, load-balanced authentication proxies presenting different source IPs."

  events:

    $auth1.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth1.principal.user.userid != ""
    $auth1.principal.ip != ""
    not $auth1.principal.user.userid in %global_allowed_shared_accounts
    not $auth1.principal.ip in %global_allowed_auth_proxy_ips

    $auth2.principal.user.userid != ""
    $auth2.principal.ip != ""

    $auth1.principal.ip != $auth2.principal.ip

    $auth1.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $auth2.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

    platform = "Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi"
    false_positives = "Software deployment agents (SCCM, Ansible, Chef, Puppet) writing installers to temp directories; developer toolchains (npm, pip, cargo) caching packages; legitimate RMM tools staging updates; CI/CD runners; container image build processes."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target: executable or script file extensions across all supported platforms
    // Windows PE, scripts, archives with embedded payloads; Linux/macOS ELF, scripts; ESXi VIBs
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(exe|dll|sys|bat|cmd|ps1|vbs|js|hta|msi|msp|jar|py|sh|bash|zsh|pl|rb|elf|bin|run|so|dylib|vib|esxpkg|pkg|deb|rpm|appimage|phar|wsf|scr|cpl|ocx|xll|wsh)$/ nocase

    // Windows: temp, downloads, appdata, public, recycle, programdata staging
    // Linux/macOS: /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /run, home subdirs
    // ESXi: /tmp, /scratch, /vmfs/volumes staging paths
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/](temp|tmp|temporary internet files)[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]downloads[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]appdata[\\\/](local|roaming)[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]users[\\\/][^\\\/]+[\\\/](desktop|documents|music|videos|pictures)[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]programdata[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]public[\\\/]/ nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/tmp\// nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/tmp\// nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/dev\/shm\// nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/run\// nocase or

      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/scratch\// nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/vmfs\/volumes\// nocase or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/opt\/[^\/]+\/tmp\// nocase
    )

    // Writing process is a network-capable or scripting process, not a known installer
    // Matches curl, wget, python, powershell, wscript, mshta, certutil, ftp, scp, sftp, rsync, finger, bitsadmin, etc.
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /[\\\/](curl|wget|python[23]?|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|certutil|bitsadmin|ftp|scp|sftp|rsync|finger|tftp|nc|ncat|netcat|socat|php|ruby|perl|node|nodejs|bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|tcsh|csh|busybox|lwp\-download|aria2c|axel|httpie|http|fetch|winhttp|xh)$/ nocase

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_staging_writers

    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good sync processes to %global_allowed_credential_readers. Add approved internal sync destinations to %global_allowed_credential_sync_destinations. Scope by tenant if a specific password manager is universally deployed."

  events:

    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

  condition:
    $file and $net
}

          and
          re:match($e1.principal.process.command_line, `(cl|clear|sl|set-log|delete|stop|disable|update)\s+`, nocase)
          and
          re:match($e1.principal.process.command_line, `(security|system|application|microsoft-windows-sysmon|microsoft-windows-windows defender|microsoft-windows-sense|microsoft-windows-etw|powershell|windefend)`, nocase)
        )
        or
        // PowerShell disabling Windows Defender or security features
        (
          re:match($e1.principal.process.command_line, `(Set-MpPreference|Add-MpPreference|Remove-MpPreference|Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature|Uninstall-WindowsFeature)`, nocase)

      and
      (
        re:match($e2.target.registry.registry_key, `(HKLM|HKCU)\\(SOFTWARE|SYSTEM)\\`, nocase)

      )
    )

  condition:
    $e1 or $e2 or $e3

}
